transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda - run through the numbers from the benchmark runs we did last night, talk tuning, and decide next steps. Maya and I will go through the spreadsheet.
[00:12] Dr. Priya Rao: Great, thanks Alex. we mostly care about p95 under our live-ish mix and also sustained throughput, that’s the big two for us.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Yep, understood. quick note, the runs compare Redwood hosted default config, Redwood with batching/cache tuned, and your baseline provider runs (OtherCloudAI) using the config you shared last week. there are a couple of caveats I'll call out as we go.
[00:35] Ethan Brooks: one thing up front - baseline traces are the ones we pulled from bucket, we didn't have the provider's raw latency histo, just the client-side measurements. so there might be small differences.
[00:46] Alex Chen: good call Ethan. ok Maya, take it away.
[00:48] Maya Patel: all right, slide one - overall p50/p95 numbers for the 512-token workload. Redwood hosted out-of-the-box p95 was 320ms, tuned Redwood with batching and prefix cache down to 210ms p95; baseline provider reported p95 ~320-360ms depending on run. p50 numbers were 70ms tuned vs 95ms baseline.
[01:15] Dr. Priya Rao: so that's like 30% p95 improvement when tuned?
[01:18] Maya Patel: roughly, yeah. for 512 tokens, about 30% improvement at p95 and 20-25% lower cost per token after batching.
[01:26] Lena Ortiz: what's the throughput numbers? our target is 120 QPS sustained with occasional spikes to 250 QPS.
[01:32] Maya Patel: good question. on single model instances, Redwood sustained ~140 qps with 1.5x concurrency, and with batching across a small pool we hit 260 qps burst capacity with 10% higher latency. baseline provider peaks were around 150 qps but had higher tail spikes - more variability.
[01:50] Alex Chen: to be clear, these are hosted numbers on the same instance class you provisioned for the POC right?
[01:55] Maya Patel: yes, same instance SKU we agreed on - 4 A100 equivalents (note: transcription sometimes shows instance names slightly different). we also ran a quantized model variant (int8-ish) - that reduced latency another ~15% but we saw a mild quality delta on a small subset of prompts.
[02:12] Dr. Priya Rao: quality delta how big - is it tolerable? we can't compromise accuracy for triage classification of notes.
[02:19] Maya Patel: for the top-line prompts we care about, difference was minor; for edge-case generation tasks it showed slight phrasing changes. recommend running a focused eval on your golden prompts before switching quantization in prod.
[02:32] Ethan Brooks: any notes about KV/prefix cache behavior? our workload has a lot of repeated prefixes.
[02:36] Maya Patel: yes - enabling prefix/KV cache reduced token compute by ~25% for sessions with repeated history. p95 for multi-turn flows dropped from ~480ms to ~290ms with cache enabled. that was a big win for chat-heavy flows.
[02:53] Lena Ortiz: was that cache per-instance or global? how does it play with autoscaling?
[02:58] Maya Patel: it's per-pool cache with warmed entries across GPUs in the pool; autoscaler keeps a minimal number of warm nodes and we have a warm-start policy to avoid cold-cache tail latency. we can tune the warm pool size to balance cost.
[03:12] Alex Chen: quick call-out on cost: with batching + cache + quantization the cost per 1M tokens in our configs dropped about 22% vs baseline provider in these runs. numbers vary by model and prompt length.
[03:23] Dr. Priya Rao: ok that's meaningful. can you share the raw cost calc?
[03:26] Alex Chen: yes I'll share the spreadsheet with the line-item calc.
[03:29] Maya Patel: another caveat - baseline provider runs had slightly different sequence length distribution; we normalized but some residual skew remains which can bias throughput.
[03:38] Ethan Brooks: noted. also we had one weird run where the baseline showed a long tail ~1.2s p95 - not sure if that was noisy network or instance contention.
[03:46] Alex Chen: we saw that too in one of the baseline snapshots; we suspect multi-tenant noisy neighbors on the provider side during that run.
[03:52] Dr. Priya Rao: switching gears - private deployment. we need to understand how these numbers translate to a VPC/on-prem deployment. any early guidance?
[04:01] Maya Patel: great question. in Private deployments you get more predictable isolation so tail latency is generally better. our internal runs on dedicated pools showed p95 similar to tuned hosted numbers, sometimes 10-15% lower tails because of less interference. main differences are network egress and the customer's infra variability.
[04:18] Lena Ortiz: network egress - would that add like 50-100ms?
[04:21] Maya Patel: it depends on coloc, but often 10-40ms extra for cross-az egress; within same colo it's lower. we can co-locate controllers closer to your API gateway to minimize that.
[04:32] Dr. Priya Rao: security questions - SOC2, KMS, audit logs - you mentioned audit logs in the doc, are they present in the POC?
[04:38] Alex Chen: yes we have audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC and KMS integration options for Private. for hosted POC we can provide redacted audit logs and support a SOC2 package review. I'll attach security docs in the follow-up.
[04:51] Ethan Brooks: any blocking points for us to run the private pilot next month? we need an estimate of infra footprint and cost delta.
[04:58] Maya Patel: we'll provide an estimated node count mapping from your QPS targets and target p95 - that'll be in the config proposal I'm delivering. cost delta depends on commitment level (dedicated vs reserved) but we'll show it in the spreadsheet.
[05:09] Lena Ortiz: back to tuning - what specific batching params did you change? we tried increasing batch size earlier and saw worse tails.
[05:16] Maya Patel: we recommend request-latency-bucketed batching with dynamic batch cutoff, plus per-model max batch size tuned by sequence length. for your workload we set max batch size to 64 and 40ms batch wait cutoff which gave best tradeoff; static large batches increase p95 for short prompts.
[05:33] Dr. Priya Rao: can you run an A/B where half traffic uses tuned settings and half baseline, so we can eyeball quality + latency in production?
[05:40] Alex Chen: yes that's possible with a canary rollout; Redwood Console supports per-route rollouts. we can coordinate traffic split and collect eval metrics on your golden set.
[05:49] Ethan Brooks: about the raw traces - we'll link the S3 bucket to your team but read-only. expected by when?
[05:54] Alex Chen: try to get access by Monday; I'll follow up with a short email.
[05:59] Maya Patel: ok next steps recap - I'll draft the config (batching/quant) and propose node/warm-pool sizing; Alex will share the spreadsheet and security docs; Priya/Ethan will send traffic profile and grant access to baseline traces.
[06:14] Lena Ortiz: timeline wise we'd like to get a private pilot spun up by mid-May if possible.
[06:19] Alex Chen: that's doable - depends on infra lead times. we'll flag any long lead items in the follow-up.
[06:25] Dr. Priya Rao: one last Q on competitor beat - you mentioned OtherCloudAI had more tail variance, any idea cause?
[06:31] Maya Patel: likely multi-tenancy and less aggressive KV caching; they also had different batching defaults that favored latency for short seqs but hurt throughput.
[06:40] Alex Chen: okay if no other questions we'll wrap. thanks everyone.
[06:44] Dr. Priya Rao: thanks all, useful.
[06:46] Ethan Brooks: thanks.
[06:47] Alex Chen: I'll send the follow-up with files and propose a deep-dive slot for private deployment.
[06:52] END TRANSCRIPT
